summary: Intermittent 5xxs caused by API gateway thin-pool backlog and runtime eviction spikes
description:
Issue summary: Customers (NovaAssist) observed intermittent 502/503 responses for generation and streaming endpoints across multiple tenants. The errors started during a midday traffic shift and clustered around a short period of sustained prefetch-heavy traffic.

Impact: Multiple requests returned 5xx (~2-4% error rate over a 30m window) resulting in degraded product experience for NovaAssist customers on dedicated capacity. Latency also increased for some long-poll streaming sessions.

Timeline: 2026-03-13 11:34 UTC - first reports from NovaAssist via support token. 11:40 - monitoring alert: apigw 5xx rate > 1.5%. 11:44 - SRE paged. 11:52 - temporary mitigation (rate-limits + scale) applied.

Environment: prod/us-east dedicated fleet for NovaAssist. Affected routes include /v1/generate and /v1/stream.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Reproduce traffic pattern: sustained prefetch + N concurrent long-lived streaming sessions (keepalive every 15s). 2) Observe apigw accept queue and thin-pool metrics rising. 3) Hit generation endpoint with medium-size prompts (avg 600 tokens).

Observed behavior: Apigw accept backlog increases to the configured thin-pool limit, new connections experience 502; serving-runtime shows GPU eviction spikes and several runtimes exited with SIGSEGV around the same window. Prefetch workers reported persistent thread exhaustion and high memory growth in heap profiles.

Expected behavior: Requests should be queued gracefully or retried without amplifying to runtime restarts. Runtime should avoid GPU eviction cycles under this load pattern.

Relevant logs/metrics: apigw.accept_queue.length spiked to 1200 (configured soft limit 1024); apigw.5xx_rate peaked at 3.9%. runtime.gpu.evictions spiked with correlating OOM logs and SIGSEGV stack dumps at 0x7fffa3. Heap profiles from prefetcher show sustained growth over 20 minutes.
investigation:
Initial hypothesis: combination of prefetch worker leak + connection backlog causing apigw thin-pool saturation which amplifies retries and forces the serving runtime into memory pressure and GPU eviction.

What we checked:
- Correlated apigw metrics with runtime restarts (trace id map).
- Collected heap profiles from prefetcher and runtime core dumps from the two affected containers. Heap profiles show unbounded list growth in prefetcher request context objects.
- Kernel logs show repeated NVidia driver notifications about memory pressure prior to evictions.
- Tracing indicates a high rate of prefix prefetch requests for NovaAssist tenant between 11:20-11:50 UTC.

Partial findings:
- Prefetcher threadpool saturated: live threads == max threads and queue length in worker pool trending to max backlog.
- Prefetcher memory retention appears to be caused by a not-cleared metadata cache (pat: prefetchCache.entries not trimmed under high-concurrency).
- Apigw thin-pool accept backlog fill resulted in 502 responses instead of graceful backpressure due to a short-circuit path in the proxy when backlog >= hard_limit.
- Runtime crash (SIGSEGV) likely secondary to GPU eviction under memory pressure; core dump suggests an invalid pointer in kv-cache eviction path (stack trace attached to INT-482).

Next investigative steps: enable verbose prefetcher GC logging for the pool, collect further heap profiles at 1m intervals, and reproduce in staging with a synthetic traffic script to validate the backlog->eviction path.
actions_taken: 11:55 UTC - Applied ad-hoc rate limit on NovaAssist tenant route (30 rps) to reduce prefetched concurrency
12:02 UTC - Scaled prefetcher worker pool for NovaAssist to 3x (temporary) to drain backlog
12:10 UTC - Restarted 2 affected runtimes in the pool (rolling restart) to clear corrupted state
12:25 UTC - Adjusted apigw accept queue soft_limit to 2048 while we triage (temporary)
12:40 UTC - Opened PR https://github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/658 to fix prefetchCache trimming and add defensive checks in kv-cache eviction

resolution_notes:
Workaround implemented: temporary rate limit and scaled prefetcher pool reduced immediate 5xx rate to baseline. Rolling restarts cleared corrupted runtime state. Long-term fix: merge PR 658 (prefetchCache trim + kv-cache defensive guards), add circuit-breaker path in apigw to return 429 instead of 502 when accept backlog crosses soft limit, and harden runtime eviction logic to avoid SIGSEGV on eviction race.

Follow-ups:

- Instrumentation: add prefetch cache size alert and apigw backlog graceful-fail metric (owner: Marco Ruiz, target 2026-03-17).
- Postmortem: write-up and impact analysis for NovaAssist and update runbook (owner: Aisha Patel, target 2026-03-20).
